title: Visualizing impurity-driven scattering phase textures in EuCd2As2
authors: Raquel Sánchez-Barquilla, Rafael Pineda Medina, Pablo García Talavera, Adrian Valadkhani, Edwin Herrera, Brinda Kuthanazhi, Lin-Lin Wang, Sergey L. Bud'ko, Paul C. Canfield, Roser Valentí, Isabel Guillamón, William J. Herrera, Alfredo Levy Yeyati, Hermann Suderow
abstract: Understanding how disorder modifies electronic states in magnetic semiconductors is important for controlling spin-dependent transport and topological responses. Here we use scanning tunneling microscopy to visualize scattering phase textures in EuCd2As2. By isolating a single surface wavevector we reconstruct spatial phase maps of the local density of states and identify phase dislocations characterized by 2pi winding around impurity sites. These phase singularities emerge systematically within charge puddles generated by Eu interstitials and their positions evolve with bias voltage. We show that their spatial structure is consistent with interference between multiple scattering channels, including contributions from spin-orbit coupling. We provide a model which reproduces phase dislocations and relates the decay of the phase gradient to the relative strength of spin-orbit and scalar scattering. Our results establish a route to access the phase of electronic scattering in real space and study the role of local disorder and spin-orbit interactions in shaping electronic states in quantum materials.
summary: This work uses STM to map the electronic scattering phase in the magnetic semiconductor $	ext{EuCd}_2	ext{As}_2$. By identifying phase dislocations around impurities, the researchers provide direct evidence of spin-orbit coupling effects in real space. This technique offers a novel way to study how local disorder shapes the electronic structure in quantum materials.
main_problem: The study aims to understand how structural disorder modifies electronic states in magnetic semiconductors by visualizing the scattering phase in real space.
main_result: The research successfully visualizes phase dislocations, characterized by $2\pi$ phase windings around impurity sites, which are signatures of spin-orbit coupling interference.
method: Scanning Tunneling Microscopy (STM) is used to measure the local density of states (LDOS), from which the spatial phase of the electronic scattering is extracted via Fourier filtering.
model_or_system: The physical system is the magnetic semiconductor $	ext{EuCd}_2	ext{As}_2$, which exhibits disorder due to $	ext{Eu}$ interstitials. The analysis models the LDOS modulation to isolate and map the phase $\phi(\mathbf{r})$.
key_observables: Phase dislocations (phase slips), spatial phase maps $\phi(\mathbf{r}, V)$, and the decay length of the phase gradient.
important_parameters: Bias voltage ($V$), magnetic field (0 T vs 14 T), and the relative strength of spin-orbit coupling ($	ext{t}_{	ext{SO}}$) versus scalar scattering ($	ext{t}_0$).
main_assumptions: The LDOS can be modeled as an amplitude- and phase-modulated cosine, and the analysis relies on isolating a single scattering wavevector $\mathbf{q}_0$.
figures_summary: Figures show STM topography revealing charge puddles, and corresponding phase maps ($\phi(\mathbf{r}, V)$) clearly displaying phase slips concentrated near impurity sites.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the necessity of phase mapping to observing phase slips near impurities, developing a model linking phase winding to SOC, and finally quantifying the SOC influence via the decay length of the phase gradient.
why_interesting: The ability to map the phase of electronic scattering in real space provides a powerful, direct diagnostic tool for studying spin-orbit coupling effects in disordered quantum materials, bridging concepts from topological physics and local disorder physics.
